findings.summary: Verified: forrest-1864-03-27 reads 'attacked it on the evening of the 26th' (p.607) and Hicks prints Forrest's demand 'Headquarters Forrest’s Cavalry Corps, Paducah, Ky ., March 25, i864.' (p.547), each occurring once. KY010 recorded-result value now states the conflict with the frozen March 25, Hicks's '25th instant' and the printed demand, with both citations; the date is kept, not reconciled. The family note and the memo's Dates bullet say the same.

Verified in nps-ky011-v1 Description: 'Altogether, Morgan had about 1,300 Union prisoners of war camping with him overnight in line of battle.' KY011 casualty-records records it with the NPS citation. The 'presumably includes' inference is replaced by the review's wording: NPS's 1,300 and Morgan's 400 and 1,500 (or 2,000) bear on the frozen Union 1,092, but no inspected source states its basis. The memo is updated.

Verified in washburn-1864-09-02 (p.470): dispatch No. 2 to A. J. Smith, 'He has 500 prisoners, I think, but failed to take the battery'. TN031 casualty-records value, rationale (Washburn about 250 and 500; Forrest 400; NPS 500; Jordan some 600; none adopted) and memo updated as proposed, with the citation added.

Verified in breckinridge-1865-01-03 postscript (p.827): the 'not more than twenty' follows the exclusion of Vaughn's and Duke's commands (no report yet) and of the citizens who made up most prisoners. VA081 casualty-records value rewritten to that scope, with the postscript sentence cited. The memo's Casualties bullet now gives the scope.
Same verification as VA081-R1. VA082 casualty-records no longer says 'twenty of his men ... in the whole expedition'; it gives the review's scoped wording and cites the same postscript sentence.

Verified in nps-tn030-v1 Description: 'The garrison was unable to depress its artillery enough to cover the approaches to the fort' (occurs once). The citation is added to bluff-fort-and-commanding-ground; the value is unchanged.

Verified: Inclosure No. 4 is headed 'JOHN W. GLADDEN’S STATEMENT' (p.13). 'Refugee' is Thomas's word ('a statement of a refugee from Dalton'), just after the selected range in the pinned parent OCR (collapsed offset 45,251). reported-force-scope, transport-and-forage, casualty-records and the family note are reworded as proposed, the inclosure heading is cited, and the memo is updated. The optional metadata-only revision of or32-1-thomas-dalton-selections-v1.dependency_note ('with a refugee's statement') is not made; that decision is left to the primary.
Memo only: the AL002 family cell reads '3 (Rawlins's dispatch not independent of Dodge)'.

AL002 reported-force-scope rationale and memo: the frozen force field's 1st Alabama Cavalry [CS] and Dodge's 'Patterson's and Hannon's regiments' are named differently and not reconciled. Both passages were already cited.

In part. Verified in forrest-1864-02-26 (p.350). MS013 casualty-records adds Forrest's '6 pieces of artillery, 100 killed, over 100 prisoners, and wounded estimated at 300 or over' for the two days' pursuit from West Point, with its scope cited. Sherman's March 7 'unpardonable' (verified in sherman-1864-03-07) goes into MS013 open_questions, not used, because it would be a fourth family and does not close the record's most consequential gap.

As notes only. The compiler footnote after Johnston's Dalton excerpt ('Portion of report here omitted will appear in connection with the Atlanta campaign, Vol. XXXVIII, Part II'), verified in parent OCR, lies outside the selection, so it is recorded in GA006's family note and the memo with the Part II/Part 3 mismatch unreconciled, not cited. The unselected footnote to the Inclosure No. 5 'Total*' row is listed as deferred.
Verified in sturgis-1864-06-24 (p.95). MS014 reported-force-scope and memo add the captured sergeant's 12,000 engaged and two infantry divisions in reserve; not adopted.

Verified in ajsmith-1864-08-05 (p.253). MS015 reported-force-scope and memo add Smith's 'numbering perhaps 1,000 men' at Old Town Creek (inside the frozen July 14-15 interval) as a scoped estimate; not adopted.

Verified in leaming-1865-01-17 (p.561). TN030 killing-after-assault adds, as Leaming's statement, that when the lines were broken one company of the Sixth U.S. Heavy Artillery (colored troops) rushed down the bluff and many jumped into the river throwing away their arms, before the garrison surrendered. Two citations are added. Nothing is adopted in the claim's own voice; status stays disputed.

Verified in leaming-1865-01-17 (p.562). TN030 killing-after-assault records, attributed and quoted, Leaming's statement that subsequent events show Bradford 'was brutally murdered the first night of his capture'. For balance it cites Forrest's April 15 letter to Davis, which mentions Bradford's capture and not his fate. The rationale says Leaming's statement rests on unspecified events and that Bradford's fate is not adopted. It is placed in the killing claim, not command-roles.

Verified in hicks-1864-04-06 (p.548): 'all of whom, with one exception, were convales- cents in the general hospital, and too feeble to get to the fort.' Added beside the 35-40 figure in KY010 casualty-records and in the memo.

Verified in burbridge-1864-08-01 (pp.26-27). KY011 casualty-records and memo now say that the list is the total of the brigade reports for 'the loss of my immediate command', and that its footnote says many of the missing had since returned. Both are cited.
Verified in the Jordan memphis-expedition selection (p.543). TN031 reported-force-scope and memo add that the infantry Neely attacked was 'at least a thousand strong'; not adopted.

Verified in breckinridge-1865-01-03 (p.826). The 200 prisoners and 'at least 8'00 horses' are added to VA082 casualty-records only, where the adjacent Saltville retreat passage is already cited, to avoid double counting. The rationale marks them as expedition context not assigned to the record. The memo is updated.

Dossier and memo only. Echols's No. 9 was re-read in parent OCR (no account of the shootings; it says two or three Black regiments were 'badly cut up'), and Williams's No. 11 and Vaughn's No. 12 were keyword-searched. The VA076 rationale now names the Confederate reports read and says they give no account of these events. McLean's No. 4 itinerary is not recorded as read in any inspection note, so it is listed as deferred. The registry inspection field of or39-1-gardner-saltville-selections-v1 is not revised (immutable; optional).

Verified in the frozen cwsac_battles description for VA076 ('On the morning of October 1, ...'). VA076 recorded-result says the frozen description itself dates the attack to October 1 and cites it; the memo is updated.

As notes only. The compiler footnote (parent OCR, outside the selection) records a duplicate dated October 18, 1864, co-signed by Assistant Surgeon J. T. Harper. It is noted in VA076 open_questions and the memo, and the null-mapped date is kept. No registry revision (immutable; optional).

Verified: breckinridge-1864-11-29 'on the CA^ening of the 11th of November' (p.892) and Gillem's 'arrived at 7 a. m. of the 10th' and 'morn¬ ing of the 10th [11th]' (p.888). The TN033 recorded-result rationale states the conflict with all three cited. command-roles now follows the passive 'An attack for the next morning was arranged' instead of 'Breckinridge says he arranged'. The memo is updated.

No change. The one-day extensions past KY010's and TN030's single-day frozen intervals are already disclosed in the boundary notes and tagged post_outcome, with nothing added to casualties. The Forrest West Tennessee memo notes that they must stay explicit if these records are later bounded for features.
No action required by the review. The wrong NPS Campaign fields are already noted in the NPS inspection records and not adopted; each memo's review section says so.
